claims.text: GPT-3.5 achieved an F1-score of 0.78 for depression detection on the Distress Analysis Interview Corpus-Wizard of Oz dataset.
Emotion-aware BERT Tiny achieved 93.14% accuracy in sentiment analysis.
Emotion-aware BERT Tiny achieved 85.46% accuracy in emotion analysis.
PsychBERT achieved an F1-score of 0.63 in classifying mental health syndromes across social media and academic literature datasets.
BERTimbau large achieved an accuracy of 0.955 in detecting suicidal ideation in Portuguese text.
ChatGPT achieved a higher mean empathy rating (3.64) than physicians (3.13) when responding to autism-specific questions.
Translating personal conversation databases from English into Polish decreased emotion categorization task accuracy from 90% to 80%.
GPT-4 Turbo suggested medication options that were contraindicated or considered less efficient choices by experts in 12% of evaluated clinical cases.

In a review of 40 articles on LLMs in mental health, 38% focused on text-based detection of conditions and suicidal ideation, 18% on conversational agents, and 45% on other clinical applications and evaluations.
98% of the evaluated studies on LLMs in mental health investigated BERT or GPT model variants.

evidence.description: Danner et al achieved F1-scores of 0.53 and 0.59 using a CNN on the DAIC-WOZ dataset, whereas GPT-3.5 achieved an F1-score of 0.78.
Emotion-aware BERT Tiny achieved an accuracy of 93.14% in sentiment analysis, outperforming baseline models.
Emotion-aware BERT Tiny achieved an accuracy of 85.46% in emotion analysis tasks.
PsychBERT achieved an F1-score of 0.63, outperforming traditional CNN (0.57) and LSTM (0.51) networks.
Diniz et al showed that BERTimbau large reached 0.955 accuracy, 0.961 precision, and 0.954 F1-score in detecting Portuguese suicidal ideation text.
In 717 evaluations across 239 questions, ChatGPT achieved a mean empathy score of 3.64 compared to 3.13 for physicians.
Zygadlo et al noted that machine translating personal conversation databases from English to Polish caused performance to drop from 90% accuracy in English to 80% in Polish.
Perlis et al demonstrated that GPT-4 Turbo recommended medications deemed less efficient or contraindicated by expert clinicians in 12% of cases.
40 papers were classified into 15 (38%) on text analysis screening/detection, 7 (18%) on conversational agents, and 18 (45%) on other applications and evaluations.
39 out of 40 reviewed papers (98%) focused on BERT and its variants or GPT models as primary models studied.

methodologies.name: PRISMA Systematic Literature Search and Selection
methodologies.description: Systematic review following PRISMA guidelines querying 5 open-access databases for peer-reviewed studies published between 2017 and 2024 on LLMs in mental health.
conditions: Keyword query: (mental health OR mental illness OR mental disorder OR psychiatry) AND (large language models)

methodologies.name: Interrater Reliability Assessment and Risk of Bias Evaluation
methodologies.description: Dual independent reviewer screening evaluated via Cohen kappa statistics combined with quality and bias evaluation using the Risk of Bias 2 tool.

limitations.text: The systematic review search was limited strictly to English-language publications.
The evaluation covers a limited diversity of LLMs, with 98% of reviewed literature focusing on BERT variants and GPT models.
The review period ends in April 2024 and cannot capture subsequent rapid developments in LLM technologies.
Social media datasets used for text-based mental health screening contain demographic age bias towards younger populations.
Scarcity of annotated mental health datasets in non-English languages degrades model performance when relying on machine translation.
LLMs lack interpretability due to their black-box nature, generate hallucinatory or inconsistent text, and lack a benchmarked clinical ethical framework.

future_work.text: Train specialized LLMs for mental health using expert-annotated, diverse demographic datasets and specialized clinical lexicons.
Integrate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to supply up-to-date evidence-based facts and mitigate hallucinations in clinical dialogs.
Incorporate privacy-enhancing technologies such as differential privacy, zero-knowledge proofs, federated learning, and token masking to protect patient data.
Collaborate with regulators, AI researchers, clinicians, and policy makers to build benchmarked ethical frameworks and accountability standards for healthcare AI.
